insight: npm run build rewrites next-env.d.ts imports from .next/dev/types to .next/types (and next dev flips it back). The file is committed, so a verification build dirties the tree. Revert it with git checkout -- next-env.d.ts before pushing rather than committing the churn.

NSP had no VERSION file, so gstack-version-bump classify returns DRIFT_UNEXPECTED (a false positive: it compares package.json 0.1.0 against an absent VERSION treated as 0.0.0.0). Not a manual-edit bypass. As of v0.1.0.1 VERSION and CHANGELOG.md exist, so classify should return FRESH from here on.

playwright.config.ts starts its own dev server on port 3017 with reuseExistingServer:false, so npx playwright test needs no manual server and will not collide with npm run dev on 3000. Full suite runs in about 5 seconds.
